qualification.demandAndDistinctness: The HVA Berkshire guide publishes upper mainstem Sections A, B, C, E, and F, with named access points, distances, difficulty, dam boundaries and route descriptions. The three upper source-defined sections keep standalone pages; composite upper and lower combinations remain selectable on the hub with their own endpoints and safety notes. Stockbridge and Great Barrington/Sheffield retain separate access choices because the dams, portage, launch grade, water character and public take-outs are materially different.
qualification.scoring: All fifteen routes use a minimum-only scored profile with HVA’s broad 150 cfs minimum planning cue, not a safe-flow guarantee. Gauge references now vary by trip area: USGS 01197145 at Lenoxdale for the upper chain, 01197500 near Great Barrington for the Stockbridge and Division Street trips, and 01198125 near Ashley Falls for downstream Sheffield trips. The gauges are same-mainstem context but do not represent identical dams or every mile; HVA also identifies 01197000 on the East Branch at Coltsville as upstream watershed context. No high-flow score ceiling was inferred. Recheck local flow, trend, rain and route features before launch.
qualification.access: The endpoints follow HVA’s public canoe access chain: Fred Garner Park, Decker Landing, Woods Pond Bridge, Lee Athletic Field, Park Street, Glendale Dam above and below its portage, Rising Pond, Division Street, Brookside Road, East Sheffield Road, Sheffield Covered Bridge and Rannapo Road. HVA marks the former Searles/Bridge Street access closed; no route uses it as an endpoint or bailout. The Great Barrington River Walk is not a launch. The Town reports the interim Division Street bridge open after repair, with replacement work planned for fall 2026; it reports Brookside Road Bridge closed to vehicle traffic. Users are directed to check Town access status before travel. The August 20, 2026 East Sheffield stabilization closure was a scheduled one-day work window and has passed; current notices remain linked. Division Street, Brookside and East Sheffield landing points were refined to the adjacent canonical Housatonic water line inside independently documented access areas. Rising Pond remains within the mapped waterbody and at the HVA water-edge access; its nearest NHD flowline is 215 ft away because the take-out sits on the pond margin.
qualification.safety: Every card requires a PFD, cold-water and rescue planning, weather/rain/gauge checks, wood/strainer scouting, public-bank use and route-appropriate daylight. Section C starts with the required right-bank Woods Pond Dam portage and proceeds into Class II–III bridge rapids; Section F begins below the separate Glendale Dam public portage and includes Class III water. Section E ends above Glendale Dam. The lower itineraries do not include the closed Bridge Street site. Cards identify the severe 40%+ East Sheffield ramp grade and limited Brookside/Rannapo parking. Housatonic PCB contamination is described accurately: avoid swimming, ingestion and sediment contact, cover open cuts, and follow current state fish-consumption advice.
qualification.camping: All fifteen routes are classified campingClassification=none. They are day trips between public launch facilities; no public overnight camping is documented along the guide reaches. Cards prohibit camping at accesses or on private banks and direct overnight travelers to separately permitted lodging or campgrounds.
qualification.gallery: Three local same-river photographs cover the upper, middle and downstream Berkshire corridors. Upper routes use John Phelan’s Housatonic railroad bridge photograph at Lenox Dale (CC BY-SA 4.0); Stockbridge routes use Phelan’s Housatonic village photograph (CC BY 3.0); lower Great Barrington/Sheffield routes use MayorBatman’s actual Housatonic at the Old Covered Bridge photograph (CC BY-SA 4.0). The app files are 1,600-pixel-wide copies under public/gallery/housatonic-berkshire/. Captions identify corridor context and do not imply exact endpoints or current conditions.
qualification.geometry: All 15 trips have route-scoped canonical USGS NHD geometry. Their named-river fallback is explicitly bounded to each documented put-in/take-out pair; it no longer exports disconnected portions of the full Berkshire Housatonic corridor. The full geometry audit passed with 2,876/2,889 catalog routes matched and 48 state assets. Focused coordinate audits returned OK for 36 of 37 checked endpoint/waypoint records. The remaining Rising Pond take-out is within the HVA access waterbody and was retained as a reviewed shoreline landing even though the NHD centerline is 215 ft away. Maximum route geometry snap is 220 ft at that same pond-margin landing.
qualification.consolidation: Fifteen trip options remain on the hub, grouped into the upper chain, Stockbridge dam reaches and Great Barrington–Sheffield public access chain. Nine source-defined or access-specific reaches keep standalone pages; six derived endpoint combinations now resolve to their exact trip cards, each with its own mileage, access, gauge, dam, shuttle and safety details. Section E (Park Street to above Glendale Dam) and Section F (below Glendale Dam to Rising Pond) remain separate because a land portage is required. The former Bridge Street/Searles access is closed and excluded. No reverse-direction or access-alias routes were added.

followUp: After deployment, verify the six exact trip-card redirects, all fifteen picker cards and the updated sitemap. Continue checking USGS station freshness, HVA updates, Town bridge and access notices, Brookside launch approach, East Sheffield access, dam/portage conditions, PCB sediment notices and active fish advisories. A discrepancy between some HVA rounded/published distances and the NHD trace is retained in route evidence; HVA named-reach mileage is displayed for source-defined sections and canonical mileage is shown for geometry-derived options.
